requirement: Load a bundled, reproducible synthetic demonstration dataset.
Accept versioned CSV imports for facilities, medicines, inventory and orders.
Validate columns, types, identifiers, dates, balances, duplicates and reference integrity.
Keep invalid rows out of analysis and preserve them with machine-readable rejection reasons.
Record source name, checksum, schema version, import time, row counts and validation outcome.
Display completeness, timeliness, validity and consistency by dataset and facility.
Prevent analysis when critical reference data or required periods are missing.
Calculate average daily consumption, usable stock, days of cover, delivery delay, order fulfilment and reporting completeness.
Produce deterministic 14-day and 30-day baseline risk.
Produce an evaluated ML risk score when an approved model artifact is available.
Display actual values before thresholds, targets or comparisons.
Classify risk as low, medium or high using versioned thresholds.
Show contributing factors and data-quality warnings for every alert.
Distinguish facts, derived metrics, predictions and inferred causes.
Allow filtering by facility, medicine, risk, forecast window and evidence quality.
Withhold or downgrade recommendations when minimum data-quality rules are not met.
Identify potential donors with stock above the configured safety threshold.
Calculate a proposed quantity in valid pack-size increments.
Show donor and recipient days of cover before and after the proposed transfer.
Reject recommendations that violate donor safety stock, expiry, pack-size or data-quality constraints.
Rank feasible transfers using urgency, safety, expiry and distance or cost proxy.
Require a reviewer to accept, edit or reject a recommendation with a note.
Never execute a stock transfer, order or procurement action.
Apply transparent rules to classify likely bottlenecks.
Support consumption surge, delayed delivery, partial order, insufficient order, reporting gap, discrepancy, near-expiry surplus and unknown.
Label bottlenecks as inferred unless directly confirmed by source data.
Generate a report without an LLM.
Include priority risks, evidence, proposed transfers, bottlenecks, owners and due dates.
Export a stable HTML report; PDF export may be added when layout is verified.
Label an LLM narrative as an AI-assisted draft pending human review.
Record imports, configuration version, model version, recommendations and review events.
Make audit events append-only through application workflows.
Never write secrets, tokens or raw sensitive records to logs.
Current usable stock must never be inferred from an invalid balance without a visible data-quality flag.
A donor facility must remain at or above its medicine-specific safety-stock days after a proposed transfer.
A proposed quantity must be a non-negative whole multiple of pack size.
Stock must have enough remaining shelf life for plausible use at the recipient facility.
Critical missing fields prohibit redistribution recommendations.
Zero consumption must be handled explicitly and never produce division-by-zero or infinite cover.
The ML model may rank risk but may not bypass deterministic safety constraints.
The LLM may explain approved calculations but may not create risk scores or transfer quantities.
Editing a recommendation creates a new reviewed version; it does not overwrite the original.
Every recommendation remains non-executable advisory output.
The deterministic analytical path must work when the LLM or network is unavailable.
District summary for the bundled dataset should load within 2 seconds after data is processed on a typical development laptop.
Secrets must come from environment variables or an approved secret store.
All external inputs must be validated at trust boundaries.
Logs must include correlation identifiers and structured event names.
User-facing screens must target WCAG 2.2 AA and not rely on colour alone.

requirement: Business logic must be isolated from API and UI frameworks.
Synthetic-data generation and model evaluation must be reproducible from fixed seeds and versioned configuration.
The MVP must not accept patient-level personally identifiable data.
